title: Here’s how to use intelligent dictation in Gemini for macOS.
gist: Google's Gemini app for macOS added an 'intelligent dictation' feature that transcribes natural speech into polished text in any desktop window — removing filler words, applying mid-sentence corrections, and inserting formatted text at the cursor. A thin promotional how-to post, but it signals Google pushing Gemini deeper into OS-level desktop workflows.

insights.claim: Google has shipped an intelligent dictation feature in the Gemini app for macOS that lets users create, edit, and summarize by voice directly inside any window on the desktop, not just inside the Gemini app.
insights.speaker: Google AI Blog
insights.so_what: Google is embedding Gemini at the OS-workflow layer on Apple's platform — a distribution wedge into daily desktop usage worth watching for the assistant land-grab against Apple's and Microsoft's native AI features.

insights.claim: Gemini's macOS dictation performs on-the-fly speech cleanup — automatically stripping 'ums' and 'ahs', catching mid-sentence corrections, and dropping formatted text instantly at the cursor — positioning it as a polished-output tool rather than raw transcription.

insights.so_what: LLM-grade cleanup as a default OS input method threatens standalone dictation/transcription apps and raises the bar for voice-first productivity software.
